subject: DPA: deletion scope, onshore processing, and exportability
messages:
From: Sara White <sara.white@fintechco.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: FinTechCo Legal <legal@fintechco.com>, Jorge Ruiz <jorge.ruiz@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on DPA deletion and onshore processing

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for sending the DPA draft. Our legal and security teams had a few items we need clarified before we can proceed:

- Deletion: can you confirm the exact deletion windows for user-provided data, model outputs, and system logs? We need a firm maximum timeframe and confirmation that deletion includes backups and snapshots.
- Onshore processing: we require processing and storage to be limited to EU data centers for EU customer data. Is there language to guarantee "EU-only" processing, and what exceptions do you allow for cross-border export?
- Exportability: in the event Redwood needs to access data for debugging, what export controls and access approvals are in place? Who has access?
- Proof: can you provide typical audit evidence or examples (logs, deletion receipts) that you would share under contract?

We'd appreciate an initial redline if possible. If some items require product changes, please note that in the response.

Regards,
Sara White
Head of Legal Operations
FinTechCo

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara White <sara.white@fintechco.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA deletion and onshore processing

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary of Redwood's position and options so we can narrow to a formal redline:

- Residency: We offer EU-hosted processing (single-region) for EU tenant data via our EU Dedicated pools or Private (VPC) deployment. We can agree to process "EU data" only within EU infrastructure; exceptions are limited and auditable.
- Deletion: standard behavior is: ephemeral cache artifacts are purged within 30 days, request-driven deletes are enacted within 48 hours started and fully realized within 30 days, and system logs are retained for debugging/monitoring up to 90 days by default. Backups and snapshots are handled separately — we can commit to removing customer-specific snapshots within 90 days after a deletion event unless otherwise required by law.
- Export/access: We can restrict cross-border exports except for narrow operational exceptions (e.g., live incident response) and those would be subject to audit logging and pre-approved personnel lists.
- Proof: we can provide deletion receipts and audit logs on request (redacted as needed). For SOC2-type evidence we can provide extracts.

I've attached an initial redline for your review (FinTechCo_Redline_v3.docx) that translates the above into proposed DPA language and flags items that would require a Dedicated/Private deployment to fully guarantee.

Looping in Mina from Security and Neha from Legal to add technical and contract specifics.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara White <sara.white@fintechco.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA deletion and onshore processing

Hi Sara, Marcus — adding technical detail from SecOps.

- Deletion semantics: there are three layers we consider: (1) application-level artifacts / model outputs (user-submitted prompts, generated outputs), (2) runtime caches/KV caches, (3) infrastructure logs and persistent backups. For EU Dedicated/Private customers we can:
  * Mark user artifacts for deletion immediately and remove from primary storage within 48 hours; secondary indices and caches are subsequently rewritten/trimmed within 7–30 days depending on workload.
  * KV/prefix caches are ephemeral by design; typical eviction is seconds–hours, but for compliance we can enforce a forced purge that sweeps caches within 30 days.
  * Backups/snapshots: encrypted snapshots exist, and deleting an object from primary storage does not instantly remove historical encrypted snapshots. Our standard commitment is deletion-from-snapshots within 90 days; for stricter requirements we can offer a contractual 45/60/90-day option tied to a Private deployment.
- Key management: customer keys via KMS/HSM are supported for Private deployments. If a customer manages keys and revokes them, that materially reduces Redwood's ability to decrypt older snapshots.
- Access controls & export: cross-border access will be limited to a named escalation roster (we recommend limiting to 3–5 engineers), all access requires just-in-time approval and is logged. Exports for debugging will only occur after documented approval and will be time-boxed.
- Evidence: we can provide time-stamped audit logs, deletion confirmation receipts, and role-based access logs. We cannot publish full historic logs for privacy reasons but can produce targeted extracts under NDA.

If you share the specific clauses you want tightened, we can suggest redline language that aligns with our operational controls.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Director, Security & Compliance
mina_haddad@redwood.com

From: Sara White <sara.white@fintechco.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: FinTechCo Legal <legal@fintechco.com>, Jorge Ruiz <jorge.ruiz@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA deletion and onshore processing

Thanks Mina and Marcus — the technical detail helps. We've reviewed your redline and proposed the following as our preferred positions (see attached redline file for inline edits):

1) Deletion windows:
  - User-submitted data & model outputs: permanent erase within 14 calendar days of a deletion request (including removal from primary indexes).
  - Runtime caches/KV caches: purge within 14 days for EU tenants.
  - System logs: retain maximum 60 days; aggregated monitoring metrics may be retained longer but must be non-reversible.
  - Backups/snapshots: customer data must be removed from backups within 90 days of deletion request; if operator-held keys prevent rapid deletion, Redwood must notify and provide expected timelines.

2) Residency/Export:
  - All processing and storage of EU customer data to occur in EU-only data centers. No cross-border export for operational debugging except under court order or explicit written consent.

3) Proof and notifications:
  - Redwood to provide deletion confirmation and a summary of which storage locations were affected within 10 business days.
  - Regulatory/legal compulsion: Redwood must notify FinTechCo within 5 business days of receiving a request to disclose EU customer data to an authority (unless prohibited by law).

We understand that some items may require a Private or Dedicated deployment; please indicate which of our points are product- or deployment-dependent. Also: we attached our redline for reference (we didn't attach the binary here — will upload if needed).

Best,
Sara White
Head of Legal Operations
FinTechCo

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sara White <sara.white@fintechco.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA deletion and onshore processing

Hi Sara — thanks for the specific asks. From a legal/contract standpoint we can propose the following compromise language that balances operability and your compliance needs:

- Residency: Redwood will process and store EU customer data in EU-only infrastructure. Exception: access by named personnel outside the EU for troubleshooting or incident response is permitted only when strictly necessary, subject to documented approvals, and limited to an agreed small roster. We can include a clause requiring prior written notice unless prohibited by law.

- Deletion timelines: proposed compromise:
  * Ephemeral artifacts & model outputs: removal from primary storage within 48 hours, full propagation to indexes/caches within 30 days.
  * System logs: 60 days retention by default (we will move to secure archival at that point); we can offer 30/60/90 options in the DPA schedule.
  * Backups/snapshots: removal within 180 days unless a Private deployment with customer-managed keys is in place (in which case we can commit to 90 days). The 180-day default is driven by operational constraints around snapshot lifecycle and disaster recovery.

- Export & legal compulsion: Redwood will object to any data export requests not legally compelled; for compelled disclosures Redwood shall notify FinTechCo within five business days where legally permissible and will limit data production to the minimum required.

- Evidence & audit: Redwood will provide deletion receipts and a summary audit log within 10 business days for each deletion request. For higher-assurance evidence we can offer an expanded audit package as a contract add-on.

If this compromise is acceptable we can turn it into formal redline language and share it back. If FinTechCo requires the 14-day hard deletion or absolute 90-day backup window without Private deployment, we should schedule a call to discuss trade-offs and any potential product changes/implementation timeline.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
